hypothesis: Adding an outer non-structural skip to LineIndex.build (src/indexer/lineIndex.ts, outside-string path just before `const b = buf[i];` at L283) that, driven by a module-level Uint8Array(256) class table WCLS marking only '"' '{' '[' '}' ']' '\n' ' ' '\t' '\r' as 1, advances i over every run of class-0 bytes in one tight do/while (setting lineHasContent = true once per run) will raise the primary speedup from ~1.50 to ~1.62-1.68, because on top of the round-2 string loop the outside-string bytes are now a large share of cost and every class-0 byte currently pays a full outer iteration + inString test + switch dispatch only to set lineHasContent = true. Unlike round 2's failed skipLHC it is not gated on lineHasContent and whitespace is folded into the table, so it skips digits/true/false/null/':'/',' runs everywhere with no extra guard. This is the only change: the string branch, the switch cases, checkpoint modulo, record pushes, for-await loop, Buffer.from conversion and EOF handling are untouched.

steps.change:
Semantics review (no edits, executor must confirm each point holds):
- Equivalence: a byte with WCLS 0 is not '"' '{' '[' '}' ']' '\n', so the old code sent it to `default`, and since it is also not 0x20/0x09/0x0d it set lineHasContent = true and did nothing else (no depth/inString/line/startOff/record change). Skipping a run of such bytes and setting lineHasContent = true once is therefore identical. Bytes > 0x7f (UTF-8 multibyte outside strings) and 0x5c outside strings are class 0 and behave as before.
- lineHasContent: set to true before advancing, only when at least one class-0 byte exists (the guard `WCLS[buf[i]] === 0` with i < n guaranteed by the while header). It is reset only by the unchanged newline case.
- Whitespace / CR: 0x20, 0x09, 0x0d are class 1, so they still go through the switch default and never set lineHasContent; whitespace-only lines and CRLF line ends ('\r' before '\n') are unchanged. '\r' in mid-line is also unchanged.
- Empty lines: '\n' is class 1, so consecutive newlines each hit the newline case with lineHasContent false -> sawMultiline = true, as before.
- Depth clamp: '}' and ']' are class 1, so `if (depth > 0) depth--;` is still the only depth decrement; '{' '[' still increment in the switch.
- Strings: '"' is class 1, so entering a string still goes through `case 0x22` (inString = true); the skip runs only when inString is false (the string branch `continue`s before reaching it).
- Chunk-boundary resume: if a class-0 run reaches the end of a chunk, `break` exits with lineHasContent already true; the next chunk restarts at i = 0 with inString false and simply re-enters the skip or the switch. No new cross-chunk state exists. chunkBase/startOff arithmetic is untouched because the newline case still sees the original i.
- EOF: the post-loop logic (startOff < totalBytes branch, dangling depth/inString branch, multiline / endsWithNewline derivation) is untouched and receives the same line, startOff, depth, inString, lineHasContent, sawMultiline values as before.
- String chunks: Buffer.from(raw) unchanged; buf[i] for 0 <= i < n is always 0-255, so WCLS lookup is in range.

Verification (no file edits): run `npm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit), `npm run lint` (oxlint), `npx prettier --check src/indexer/lineIndex.ts` and `npm test`; all must pass, including src/indexer/__tests__ and src/perf/__tests__. Then run a differential check (scratch script outside the repo) of the new LineIndex.build against the branch-2fb4bdc build on: the sealed edge fixtures, compact JSONL with numbers/true/false/null at line start and line end, pretty multi-line records, CRLF files, whitespace-only and empty lines (leading, middle, trailing), unbalanced '}' / ']' at depth 0, string open at EOF with and without trailing newline, trailing backslash at EOF, escaped quotes, unicode/emoji outside and inside strings, unterminated final line; with chunk splits whole/1/2/7/64/1000 bytes, checkpointInterval 1/3/1024, array, async-iterable and string-chunk inputs. Compare checkpoints, totalBytes, totalLines, multiline, recordEndLines, recordEndOffsets and endsWithNewline for exact equality. Finally run `node scripts/benchmark-index-build.mjs` (sealed: must NOT be edited) at least 3 times, report each run's primary score and the median; correctness must be 1 in every run. Treat bimodal ratio distributions as contention-affected and re-run.

expected_outcome.estimated_impact: +9-12% (primary ~1.62-1.68 vs current ~1.50); does not by itself reach the 1.8 target, which is expected from stacking one string scanner (swarU32 or rej4u32) in a later round
expected_outcome.rationale: After round 2's string loop, the outside-string path is still one outer iteration + inString test + switch dispatch per byte, and most non-string bytes in the fixture (numbers, literals, ':' ',') are class-0 content bytes that only set lineHasContent. A tight table-driven do/while removes that dispatch per byte. The round-3 scratch harness measured this exact candidate (skipCls) on top of the merged code at 1.119, 1.110, 1.095, 1.095 relative to the real build in the same process (raw 1.634/1.625/1.496/1.608), with mirror/real calibration 0.98-1.02, so sealed ~1.50 x 1.10 = ~1.65. It differs from round 2's failed skipLHC (0.869) by not waiting for lineHasContent (also skips line-start digits/literals, no extra guard) and by folding whitespace into the table; in the same runs skipLHC gave only 1.051/1.029 and the inline-compare skipCmp 1.066/1.039. Expected delta (~+0.15) is ~2-3x the ~±0.05-0.08 run-to-run noise, so the result is testable.

history_reference.builds_on: round_2_planner_a (merged 4x-reject string loop, 1.499) which makes outside-string bytes a larger share of cost; round_2 failure lesson for round_2_planner_b ('outer skip should only be tried stacked with a faster string loop'); research brief round_3 idea 1 (skipCls, highest-confidence single change, ~1.10x in 4/4 passes).
history_reference.avoids: Round 2's lineHasContent-gated skip form (skipLHC, 0.869) and the inline-compare form (skipCmp); bundling any string scanner (swarU32 / rej4u32 / DataView SWAR / 2-word SWAR) per H001; nextCp counter and quote-before-switch (neutral/negative in rounds 1-3); sync scanChunk kernel / index-based chunk loop (0.897 / 0.882, no effect); lazy recordEndLines and Float64Array record storage (5-20% slower); Buffer#indexOf skipping (slower, wrong for raw newlines in strings); Uint8Array class table inside strings (slower than '> 0x5c'); editing the sealed benchmark.
